subject: Renewal negotiation — usage variability and pricing guardrails
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novus-retail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Contract renewal — usage spike & options

Hi Ben,

As we approach the July renewal for Novus Retail, we've been seeing a material uptick in inference usage tied to our new product search feature (April monthly token consumption was ~2.8x previous baseline). Procurement asked me to open a conversation about renewal structure — specifically: can Redwood provide a short-term price protection or a buffer credit for the upcoming quarter while we stabilize usage?

Key asks from our side:
- A temporary price hold or discount for the first 3 months post-renewal
- One-time credit to offset the April spike (we expect usage to normalize across Q3)
- Flexibility to adjust committed tier without a full multi-year penalty if we evaluate higher run rates

Can you outline what flexibility you have? If helpful, I can loop in our procurement folks.

Thanks,
Elaine Park
VP, Platform Ops
Novus Retail

Attachment: UsageReport-Apr2027.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novus-retail.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract renewal — usage spike & options

Elaine — thanks for the clear context and the report, that helps. Short answer: yes, we have a few levers we can use to give Novus predictable economics while you stabilize.

High level options we typically propose (I summarized and attached a mutual action plan):
- Price hold + tier adjustment: keep current unit rate for 9 months after renewal, allow a one-time commit rebanding to next tier (down or up) with a pro-rated true-up period.
- Surge cushion: a one-time usage credit sized to cover exceptional spikes (we can split across quarters).
- Overage cap: soft overage cap where we cap unit price for 90 days and apply a staged credit if you exceed target by >25%.

I'm proposing the attached MAP ("MAP_Novus_Renewal_v1.pdf") as a starting point — it lays out a 9-month price hold, a $45k one-time spike credit tied to April/May overage, and a commit band reclassification option with a 60-day notice window. Hannah is looped in to approve manager-level concessions.

Next steps:
1) Tell me if a 9-month hold + $45k credit would address the stabilization window.
2) If procurement needs 12 months, call that out and we can run a quick internal review.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: MAP_Novus_Renewal_v1.pdf, UsageReport-Apr2027.csv

Subject: Re: Contract renewal — usage spike & options

Ben / Hannah — appreciate the quick turnaround and the MAP. Procurement is pushing for two specific items before sign-off: a 12-month price hold (we need visibility for FY28 planning) and an explicit overage ceiling where our unit price cannot exceed X (they're worried about runaway charges if the spike continues).

A few clarifications we need:
- How does the commit reband affect billing immediately (pro-rated or backdated true-up)?
- Can the $45k credit be applied as an invoice credit across two billing cycles?
- Would Redwood consider a hard cap (not just staged credits) on unit price for the first 90 days?

Happy to accept a counter if 12 months is a stretch. We can also take DocuSign if you prepare a short amendment.

Thanks,
Elaine

Subject: Internal: Novus renewal — recommended counter to procurement

Team — quick internal note before we reply to Novus. I read Ben's MAP and Elaine's procurement asks. My recommendation to balance retention risk and precedent:

Proposed counter (to offer externally):
- Price hold: 9 months guaranteed at current committed unit rate, followed by a review period tied to average trailing 3-month consumption.
- Extension option: if Novus signs today, we offer a 12-month administrative price hold as a stretch concession, but it requires a small incremental commitment (5% uplift to the committed token band) — effectively a short-term delta to secure a longer price window.
- Spike credit: keep $45k one-time credit; allow it to be split across two invoices as an invoice credit.
- Overage protection: implement a soft cap for 90 days — if consumption exceeds the cap by >40%, we trigger an emergency review and offer an interim reduced unit price for the next 30 days (not a hard cap). Hard caps set bad precedent and are hard to underwrite; prefer a staged remedy + escalation path.

Operational asks:
- Monica: prepare an SOW addendum and coordinate the bill-run treatment for the credit (split across two billing cycles).
- Priyom: confirm feasibility of a telemetry threshold alert we can add to Novus's account so we can proactively flag spikes for both teams.
- Ben: if Novus insists on a 12-month hard hold, escalate to me with expected revenue delta and I'll review exceptions.

I'll be copied when you reply externally; try to keep language prescriptive but reasonable.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

(Quoted: Ben's MAP summary)

Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Final counter: renewal amendment & DocuSign

Elaine / Novus Procurement — thanks for the candid asks and for taking time to review the MAP. After an internal review, here's the counter we can sign off on today: 

Final offer summary:
- Price protection: 9-month guaranteed price hold at your current committed unit rate.
- 12-month price hold (stretch): available if Novus increases committed band by 5% year-over-year; we can include that as an optional clause in the amendment.
- Spike credit: $45,000 one-time credit to be applied as invoice credits split across two billing cycles (May and June invoice).
- Overage protection: a staged protection for first 90 days — if consumption exceeds the forecasted band by more than 40% we will apply an interim reduced unit price for the subsequent 30 days and open an emergency capacity review. We are not able to provide a hard absolute cap (this creates unfavorable capacity-risk precedents).
- Commit rebanding: one-time reclassification (up or down) allowed within 60 days post-renewal with a pro-rated true-up applied to the remainder of the billing period.

Attached is the short amendment (Proposed_Amendment_DocuSign.pdf) and the MAP. If this works, please sign via the DocuSign link below; the amendment includes the optional 12-month clause that can be toggled if Novus confirms the +5% uplift.
